_comment: 15 locations. Eleven are `scene` cards (a backdrop plus clickable hotspots, hosted by the graphics window); four are `tile` maps (small grids for the danger zones). `open_when` gates a place on the tide or the clock - the Salt Steps are dry for one hour of dawn/dusk ebb and no other time, and knowing that is itself a token (t_lowebb).

maps.description: The west bank. Tar, wet rope and fish that stopped being fresh on somebody else's shift. The Patience lies against the pilings with her fenders squealing, and the tide-post beside the office reads the same mark it read yesterday.
maps.short_description: Home dock. Hesper's office, the chandlery, the Patience at her berth.

maps.description: Forty feet of tarred deck and a wheelhouse that leaks. Between here and the far bank there is nothing to do but coil rope, take fares, and listen.
maps.short_description: The crossing. Two to five passengers, and whatever they let slip.

maps.description: Low beams, low light, and a fire that has been going since before anyone here was born. This is where the shift ends and the Reach says what it actually thinks.
maps.short_description: The tavern. Cobb behind the bar, Fen in the corner, Doss wherever the talk is.

maps.description: A path of heron-stones through water that is neither river nor land. At the wrong hour the stones are under a foot of it and the path is a rumour.
maps.short_description: Toma's stilt hut, the heron-stone path, and the Kelpmother's pool.

maps.description: The island town, built on the spoil of the old city and not at all embarrassed about it. Market, scrapyard, wharf, and a stair down to the water that is only a stair twice a day.
maps.short_description: Mid-river island. Counting-house, customs, market, and the Salt Steps.

hotspots.label: The head of the Salt Steps

maps.description: Warm, dry, and smelling of ink and money. Every surface is a ledger and every ledger is the second-best copy.
maps.short_description: Ottoline's broker desk, Corvin's post, and a third stair that does not sound solid.

maps.description: A counter, a bell, and a great deal of paper nobody has read since it was filed. The cellar below holds sluice ledgers going back two hundred years.
maps.short_description: Wimble's records desk, Vosk's rooms, and a cellar that costs eight tallies.

maps.description: The east bank climbs. Stone houses, a Warden post that has not posted a Warden in six years, and a tinker's wagon that has not moved in longer.
maps.short_description: East bank hill town. Yarrow's wagon, Brack's lodge, the Warden post.

links.label: The cliff path to Croy's Lamp

maps.description: A hundred and forty steps, and at the top an old man who has kept a light burning for a river that stopped needing one.
maps.short_description: The lighthouse and the lamp room. The only working signal lamp on the Reach.

hotspots.label: Ansel Croy, in the lamp room

maps.description: Bare rock, bird noise, and a bell-house built by somebody who wanted to be difficult to visit.
The tide-gate's own house, square and stubborn against the seaward current. Somebody has been living here alone for a long time.
maps.short_description: Doon's post. Guarded in some seeds. The lawful road ends here.

hotspots.label: The plaque at the Lesser Gate

maps.description: A stair going down into water that is not there at the moment. The steps are furred with weed and the weed is dry, which it should not be.
maps.short_description: Tidal stair into the undercity. Dry one hour a tide, and not a minute more.

maps.description: Shopfronts. That is the worst of it - they are shopfronts, with sills and door-numbers, and the river has been standing in them for four hundred years.
maps.short_description: The flooded arcade of the old city. Wights at slack; gulchers and the lullhound always.

maps.description: A drum of brick the size of a church, and the sound of your own breathing arriving back at you a half-second late.
maps.short_description: The bellmaker's cistern. The knock opens it; the far door goes under the Weir.

maps.description: The machinery of the tide-gate, wet and turning and enormous. Underneath the noise of it, something is holding a note.
maps.short_description: Machinery, seals, and the Sunken Choir. The finale.
